mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, triggering corporate earnings concerns and negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >40% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.3pp over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS shows no negative correlation with SPX 20-day returns (p>0.05) in a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth exceeding 0.5% monthly (INDPRO) indicates supply-side expansion, boosting corporate output capacity and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days during expansionary phases.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% monthly over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Annualized CPIAUCSL inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting anticipated monetary tightening that depresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized rate > 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 1500 thousand units signals housing sector weakness, reducing consumer confidence and corporate revenue visibility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >40% of instances when HOUST < 1500.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payrolls growth exceeding 100,000 per month (PAYEMS) indicates labor market strength, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 100,000 per month over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth exceeding 0.5% monthly (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days during consumption-driven expansions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly over a 5-year rolling window.
